search_radius_m.description: half-width of the initial pose search window

grid_points.description: candidates per axis per search pass

max_speed_mps.description: Implausible-jump speed bound: a LIDAR pose update implying more than this is DISCARDED and the prior pose is kept.  Was 0.25, sized against the RETIRED motor's 0.156 m/s ceiling. The current drivetrain measured ~0.58 m/s at max_duty=0.5 and ~0.9 m/s open-loop (2026-08-29 bench), so the gate sat BELOW the speeds the robot actually reaches and silently froze pose whenever it went quickly.  That is not just a localization bug, it invalidated a measurement: pose was used as the independent check on encoder distance, and on run_20260829_003233 the two agreed to 0.5% (28.46 m encoder vs 28.62 m pose). Both were under-reporting -- the encoder because counts_per_rev was too high, pose because updates past 0.25 m/s were being thrown away. Two suppressed measurements agreeing is not corroboration. ~1.5x headroom over the measured 0.4 m/s closed-loop ceiling

jump_confirm_tolerance_m.description: how close two consecutive rejected candidates must be to confirm a real correction

relocalize_cost_threshold.description: Global relocalization. The local search above is a hill-climb reseeded from its own previous answer, with nothing checking whether that answer is any good in absolute terms -- so once it lands in the wrong basin it stays there for the rest of the round. Measured on run_20260907_205830 (Open, 0 laps): the estimate latched 1.5-3 m off at t=8.0 s and never came back, driving the navigator into walls for 20 escape manoeuvres and 46 s of net-zero travel.  The car cannot leave the track, so a pose whose predicted scan does not match the real one is provably wrong, and a match landing off-track is evidence the search is lost -- not a reason to stand still. Both now count toward the same streak, and crossing it re-solves position over the whole free space instead of the +-0.15 m window.  Separation measured by replaying the three hardware runs of 2026-09-07 through the localizer (see LocalizationParams): across 1945 scans NEITHER clean 3-lap run ever crossed the threshold even once, while the failed run sat at a median 0.0432. Replayed from its own corrupted pose, one relocalization took it back to a 0.0101 fit and 0% off-track beams. mean clipped squared residual (m^2), real returns only, that counts as "does not explain the scan"

relocalize_after_scans.description: consecutive bad scans before re-solving globally (~1.5 s)

relocalize_grid_step_m.description: free-space candidate spacing for the global search

relocalize_accept_ratio.description: A cost over the threshold does not always mean the POSE is lost -- it can equally mean the WALL MODEL is wrong, which during blind operation (corridor widths still being estimated) it usually does. Searching globally against a wrong model finds the best explanation of a track that is not there, so the result has to beat the local estimate by a real margin before it replaces it. Without this the balanced-128 Open sweep went 128/128 -> 127/128 (scenario 94 turned into a reverse-run) and one case lost 17 s. The hardware rescue clears it easily: 0.0101 against a 0.0432 local cost, a ratio of 0.23. global fit must cost at most this fraction of the local one
